pages.title: Welcome to Google Antigravity
pages.description: Google Antigravity offers multiple product surfaces tailored to your specific development workflow. Select the interface that best fits your needs:

pages.title: Antigravity 2.0
pages.description: As we go deeper into the agent-first era, Antigravity is evolving to further empower developers. Introducing Antigravity 2.0, a standalone desktop application tailored for managing AI agents that execute complex knowledge and coding tasks.

pages.title: Getting Started with Antigravity 2.0
pages.description: Visit antigravity.google/download to download Google Antigravity 2.0.

pages.title: Build with Google
pages.description: Antigravity 2.0 makes it seamless to build with popular Google technology stacks. We have partnered with teams across Google to create curated bundles of primitives, including Skills, MCP servers, and Editor extensions, that are pre-configured for specific ecosystems.

pages.title: Antigravity 2.0 Features
pages.description: In Antigravity 2.0, agents work in Projects (previously in Agent Manager, agents were strictly mapped to a single workspace folder).

pages.title: Models
pages.description: For the core reasoning model, Antigravity offers leading frontier models. Availability depends on your plan:

pages.title: Projects
pages.description: In Antigravity 2.0, we are transitioning from the legacy repository-centric workspace model to a more flexible and secure Project-centric model. This document outlines what Projects are, how they work, and how they differ from the original workspace structure.

pages.title: Settings
pages.description: Antigravity 2.0 features a hierarchical settings architecture designed to give you granular control over your development environment.

pages.title: Agent Settings
pages.description: Controls how the agent executes generated shell commands:

pages.title: Artifact Review
pages.description: When starting a new Agent conversation, you can choose between two primary execution modes that determine how changes are proposed and reviewed:

pages.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
pages.description: Antigravity supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP) , an open standard that lets AI agents and editors securely connect to local developer tools, databases, file parsers, and external remote APIs.

pages.title: Agent Skills
pages.description: Skills are an open standard for extending agent capabilities. A skill is a folder containing a SKILL.md file with instructions that the agent can follow when working on specific tasks.

pages.title: Rules
pages.description: Rules are manually defined constraints for the Agent to follow, at both the local and global levels. Rules allow users to guide the agent to follow behaviors particular to their own use cases and style.

pages.title: Plugins
pages.description: Plugins are namespaced bundles that allow you to extend Antigravity’s capabilities by grouping skills, rules, MCP servers, and hooks into a single package.

pages.title: Hooks
pages.description: Hooks allow you to run custom scripts or shell commands at specific points during Antigravity’s execution loop. This is powerful for enforcing custom rules, running linters, or capturing diagnostics automatically.

pages.title: Sidecars
pages.description: Sidecars are background processes that run alongside Antigravity. Antigravity manages the lifecycle of sidecars, automatically launching them and restarting them if they crash or error.

pages.title: Agent Permissions
pages.description: Antigravity uses a robust, unified permission engine to secure your environment while enabling autonomous workflows. Every sensitive operation the Agent performs is represented as a permission resource formatted as action(target) .

pages.title: Asynchronous Subagents
pages.description: Subagents are an excellent way to parallelize complex tasks and preserve the context of your main agent. Instead of executing every step serially, an agent can delegate tasks—such as running tests or performing extensive codebase searches—to dedicated subagents.

pages.title: Artifacts
pages.description: An Artifact is a structured deliverable created by the agent to accomplish its task and communicate its progress and thinking to the human user. Artifacts include rich markdown plans (Implementation Plans), code diffs, architecture diagrams, images, and browser recordings.

pages.title: Implementation Plan
pages.description: Agent utilizes the implementation plan artifact to architect changes within your codebase to accomplish a task. These plans contain technical details on what revisions are necessary and are meant to be reviewed by the user. Below is an example plan generated by the agent.

pages.title: Walkthrough
pages.description: Agent creates walkthrough artifacts when it has completed task implementation; this type of artifact includes a concise summary of the changes that have been made to remind the user of what has happened in the active conversation.

pages.title: Screenshots
pages.description: The browser subagent can take screenshots of open pages or elements on pages when it would like your review of the state of the page. This is surfaced as a tool to the agent, and you can also prompt the agent to take a screenshot of a page.

pages.title: Antigravity CLI Overview
pages.description: The Antigravity CLI is the lightweight Terminal User Interface (TUI) surface of Antigravity. It brings the same core agentic capabilities as Antigravity 2.0 (such as multi-step reasoning, multi-file editing, tool calling, and conversation history) directly to your terminal.
